page: Microsoft Azure D2s_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. Powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor running at a base clock of 2.8 GHz, this configuration provides 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 1 physical core with 2 threads. Cache hierarchy includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of shared L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI cryptographic accelerators. The instance is paired with 8.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core.

Benchmark results reflect entry-level compute capabilities constrained by the dual-vCPU ceiling. Single-threaded performance stands in the middle 50 percent of tested cloud servers, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1499.0 and a stress-ng single-core rating of 1888.79. Single-threaded gzip compression reached 28.21 GB/sec. In contrast, multi-threaded metrics such as the Geekbench multi-core score (1732.0), stress-ng multi-core (1930.87), and PassMark CPU score (2997.31) occupy the lower tiers due to the single physical core footprint. Uncached memory bandwidth measured 14.75 GB/sec for reads and 13.25 GB/sec for writes.

The D2s_v5 does not include bundled local storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring remote network-attached disks for persistent operation. This architecture delivers baseline execution capacity for small-scale background jobs, lightweight web servers, development environments, and low-traffic microservices without incurring charges for excess compute or unused local drive capacity.
description: Microsoft Azure D2s_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine configuration featuring 2 vCPUs and 8.0 GB of RAM, backed by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz. The hardware layout assigns two hardware threads on a single dedicated physical core, supported by AVX-512 and cryptographic hardware extensions. Single-core compute and data compression benchmarks register in the median tier, whereas multi-core throughput and memory bandwidth benchmarks fall into lower percentile tiers due to the dual-thread core configuration. The instance does not bundle local disk storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, relying on external network-attached storage. The D2s_v5 serves as a cost-effective resource for lightweight web serving, continuous integration runners, staging environments, and entry-level container workloads with modest memory demands.
